text: It is 3 o'clock in the morning. Most of the world is sleeping, but Vaishali's family is already awake! Her father (Babuji), brother (Bhaiya), uncle (Chacha), and mother are busy. Can you guess what they are doing so early in the morning?
Why would anyone need to wake up at 3 AM for their job? What kind of work starts before the sun even comes up? Think about where the fresh vegetables in your kitchen come from.

content.title: The Journey of Vegetables
content.description: Vegetables travel a long way! They go from Farms -> Wholesale Market (Mandi) -> Vegetable Sellers -> Our Homes.

text: Vaishali's father is a vegetable seller. Before selling new vegetables, they have to sort yesterday's leftover vegetables. Then, Babuji and Bhaiya go to the Mandi (a huge wholesale vegetable market) to buy fresh vegetables for the day.

content.definition: A large wholesale market where farmers sell their crops to shopkeepers and vendors.

content.question: Where does Vaishali's father go early in the morning to buy fresh vegetables?

content.text: Have you ever seen a vegetable cart in your street? They have to work very hard, standing in the sun all day, just so we can eat healthy food!

text: Just like vegetables, many other things we use daily (like milk and newspapers) also have a long journey before they reach our homes early in the morning.

content.text: Next time you eat a vegetable, try to draw its journey from the farm to your plate. Ask your parents where they buy your vegetables from!

text: Imagine you bought a beautiful, crisp spinach (palak) leaf, but you left it in the sun all day. What will happen to it by evening? It will become soft and dry!
Vegetable sellers stay outside all day in the heat. How do they stop their vegetables from drying up and getting spoiled?

content.title: Keeping Vegetables Fresh
content.description: Sprinkling water on vegetables helps keep them fresh and crisp in the heat.

text: To keep vegetables fresh, Vaishali's family sprinkles water on them throughout the day. They also have to sort the vegetables. The unripe or damaged ones are kept aside, while the good ones are arranged nicely on the cart (thela).

content.definition: Arranging things in groups based on their quality, size, freshness, or type.

content.question: Why do vegetable sellers sprinkle water on vegetables?
options: To keep them fresh and stop them from drying

content.text: Sometimes students think vegetables never get spoiled if kept outside. Actually, many vegetables like spinach, tomatoes, and coriander spoil very quickly and need continuous care or a refrigerator!

text: Think about how we keep food fresh at home. We use refrigerators! But vegetable sellers on the street use water and wet gunny bags (boris) instead.

content.text: Take a small leafy vegetable (like coriander). Leave one leaf in the open air, and put another inside a wet cloth. Check them after 4 hours and see the difference!
